component.name: Apache Drill
component.description: Schema-free, distributed SQL query engine for large-scale datasets. A cluster of Drillbit daemons (coordinated via Apache ZooKeeper) accepts ANSI-SQL queries over JDBC, ODBC, a REST API, and a Web UI (default port 8047) and executes them directly against data in configurable storage plugins (local/HDFS/S3 files, Hive, HBase, Kafka, MongoDB, RDBMS via JDBC, HTTP), discovering schema at query time. The threat model is a v0 DRAFT under Drill PMC review; most load-bearing claims are recorded as inferred pending PMC confirmation, with two maintainer-confirmed points (contrib/ plugins in scope; storage enumeration is by design).

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document; this file is a structured translation of it.

blueprints.name: Drill clustered deployment
blueprints.description: Intended deployment: a clustered set of Drillbits inside an operator-controlled, network-isolated cluster, queried by analytics clients over the client RPC and the Web UI/REST endpoint; queries reach configured data sources through storage plugins, as the submitting user when impersonation is enabled. Embedded single-user mode is out of scope.

assets.name: Drillbit daemon
assets.description: Accepts SQL over the user RPC (JDBC/ODBC) as the foreman, parses and plans (Calcite), and executes distributed query fragments; communicates with peers over SASL-capable control/data RPC and coordinates via ZooKeeper.

assets.name: Web UI / REST API (:8047)
assets.description: Query submission, storage-plugin configuration, profiles, and options; a high-value admin surface since it can configure storage plugins and upload dynamic UDFs.

assets.name: Storage and format plugins
assets.description: file/HDFS/S3, Hive, HBase, Kafka, Mongo, JDBC (RDBMS), and HTTP plugins, including the PMC-maintained contrib/ storage and format plugins, which carry the same connector trust surface: filesystem reads and outbound network reach driven by queries.

assets.name: Dynamic UDF layer
assets.description: Built-in functions plus runtime jar upload of dynamic UDFs: in-JVM code execution by design, admin-gated.

assets.name: ZooKeeper
assets.description: Cluster coordination store; anyone with direct ZooKeeper write access has already won and is out of model.

assets.name: Underlying data sources
assets.description: HDFS/S3, RDBMS behind the JDBC plugin, Hive, HBase, Kafka, MongoDB: each enforces its own access control, which Drill honors (via impersonation and views) rather than replaces.

zones.name: SQL/REST clients
zones.description: Clients submitting queries over JDBC/ODBC/REST/Web UI; authenticated when auth is enabled, otherwise anonymous. The primary untrusted boundary.

zones.name: Drillbit cluster
zones.description: Drillbits and ZooKeeper on an operator-controlled, network-isolated cluster network, exposed to untrusted clients only through the intended client RPC and :8047 endpoints.

zones.name: Data sources
zones.description: The configured underlying data sources; with impersonation enabled the source's own ACLs bound each query, with impersonation disabled all access runs as the Drillbit service principal.

persona.description: Submits queries over JDBC/ODBC/REST; may be authenticated or, if auth is disabled, anonymous. The in-scope adversary is an authenticated low-privilege SQL/REST client (or an anonymous one where auth-disabled is a supported posture), able to submit arbitrary SQL, set connection properties, and drive query-time file/URL access through configured plugins.
Configures storage plugins, system/session options, and security settings, and uploads dynamic UDFs via the Web UI/REST. Trusted; a finding that requires these rights is out of model.
When impersonation is enabled, the Drillbit accesses the underlying data source as the submitting user, delegating authorization to the data source.
Another node in the cluster, authenticated over the inter-Drillbit RPC and fully trusted once authenticated; Drill makes no cross-node integrity claim against a Byzantine authenticated peer.

assumptions.description: A JVM on each Drillbit and ZooKeeper for coordination; the cluster network is operator-controlled and not directly exposed to untrusted clients except through the intended client RPC and :8047 endpoints.
Authorization correctness depends on the data sources (and/or Drill views plus impersonation) enforcing access; Drill does not re-implement source-side ACLs.

Beyond listening on its RPC/Web ports, reading configured storage plugins, writing query profiles and spill files to configured areas, and coordinating via ZooKeeper, a Drillbit is assumed to make no other outbound connections except those a query explicitly drives (pending maintainer confirmation).

The security envelope is set by runtime configuration: auth (drill.exec.security.auth), impersonation, wire encryption, Web UI auth, and dynamic UDF support; the shipped defaults (believed disabled for auth/impersonation/encryption) and whether a multi-user deployment left at defaults is VALID or operator misconfiguration are open wave-1 maintainer questions.

Tests, examples, sample data, embedded single-user mode, and the client-side connectors (JDBC/ODBC drivers, C++ client) are out of scope; contrib/ storage and format plugins are in scope (maintainer-confirmed).

threats.name: Unauthenticated query execution against an auth-enabled cluster
threats.description: With drill.exec.security.auth enabled, no SQL or REST statement should run before the session authenticates via the configured mechanism (PLAIN via PAM/LDAP, Kerberos, or custom); unauthenticated execution against an auth-enabled cluster is a security-critical violation.

threats.name: Low-privilege client reads data outside its authorization
threats.description: A query should read or write only what the effective identity is permitted at the data source (impersonation on) and/or what Drill views and storage permissions allow; a low-privilege client reading unauthorized data or bypassing a view is a security-critical, CVE-class violation. Note the maintainer-confirmed non-finding: enumerating and reading the files, schemas, and storage systems Drill is pointed at is the function of a federated query engine, in-model only when access crosses the authenticated identity's authorization.

threats.name: Non-admin client reaches code execution or plugin reconfiguration
threats.description: Registering UDFs and configuring storage plugins are admin-gated; a plain SQL client causing code execution, a plugin change, or arbitrary file or URL access beyond its authorization is a security-critical violation.

threats.name: Identity spoofing via connection properties
threats.description: A client must not be able to assume an arbitrary user identity through JDBC/ODBC connection properties (inbound impersonation targets) unless the operator configured a proxy/impersonation policy permitting it; an ungated identity spoof is critical.

threats.name: MITM on unencrypted client or inter-Drillbit links
threats.description: A network man-in-the-middle between client and Drillbit, or between Drillbits, where wire encryption (SASL / SSL-TLS) is not configured, can observe or alter sessions and data in the clear.

threats.name: Multi-user deployment left at auth-off / impersonation-off defaults
threats.description: If auth and impersonation ship disabled, an open, impersonation-off Drillbit exposes its service-principal access to any client: with impersonation disabled all data-source access runs as the Drill service principal and authorization collapses to whatever Drill itself enforces. Whether this posture is a VALID finding or OUT-OF-MODEL operator misconfiguration is the model's open insecure-default question; the operator responsibility to enable auth and impersonation before exposing Drill to more than one trusted user is documented either way.

threats.name: Code and connectivity execution via admin-registered UDFs and plugins
threats.description: Uploading a UDF jar or configuring a storage plugin is an authorized admin operation; the code or connection runs with the Drillbit's privileges. This is a feature, not a sandbox escape (BY-DESIGN); a finding that requires admin rights to register a UDF or add a plugin is out of model. There is no sandbox around dynamic UDFs or storage-plugin configuration.

threats.name: Query-driven SSRF and local file read through configured plugins
threats.description: The http, jdbc, and dfs plugins exist to reach URLs, RDBMSes, and filesystems, so a query can make a Drillbit issue outbound requests or read local files within the configured plugin scope; Drill provides no defense beyond what plugin configuration and impersonation bound, and restricting them is operator configuration, not an engine guarantee. In-model only if the access crosses the impersonated identity's authorization or the configured workspace.

threats.name: Cluster resource exhaustion by expensive queries
threats.description: No hard resource-fairness or anti-DoS guarantee is made (pending maintainer confirmation): a sufficiently expensive query may degrade a Drillbit through heap, direct memory, or CPU exhaustion. Whether per-query memory limits and queues bound this is an open maintainer question.

threats.name: Byzantine authenticated peer Drillbit
threats.description: A compromised Drillbit holding a valid cluster identity could behave arbitrarily over the inter-Drillbit RPC; Drill is assumed to make no cross-node integrity claim against a malicious authenticated peer (full peer trust once authenticated). Operators with cluster-host, service-account, or ZooKeeper-write access are likewise out of model.

threats.name: SQL injection in an embedding application
threats.description: An embedding application that string-concatenates untrusted input into Drill SQL has its own bug, not a Drill vulnerability. Similarly, dependency-tail CVEs from SCA scans (Calcite, Hadoop, Jackson, Netty) triage upstream unless Drill's own code reaches the vulnerable path with untrusted input.

trustBoundaries.name: Client front door trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Client to Drillbit (the foreman) over the user RPC (JDBC/ODBC) and Web UI/REST (:8047) is the primary boundary. A finding is in-model only if reachable by an authenticated low-privilege SQL/REST client (or an anonymous one where auth-disabled is a supported posture), without admin rights, data-source control, or cluster-host control.

trustBoundaries.name: Data source trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: With impersonation enabled, the Drillbit accesses the source as the submitting user and the source's own ACLs bound the query; with impersonation disabled, all access runs as the Drillbit service principal. Malformed data files from configured sources are a parser robustness concern for whoever can write the source.

controls.name: Client authentication when enabled
controls.description: With drill.exec.security.auth enabled, sessions authenticate via PLAIN (PAM/LDAP), Kerberos, or a custom mechanism before any statement runs; Web UI auth (form / SPNEGO) is tied to it.

controls.name: Authorization scoping via impersonation, views, and storage permissions
controls.description: With impersonation enabled the Drillbit accesses data sources as the submitting user, delegating authorization to the source's ACLs; Drill views and storage permissions add engine-side scoping.

controls.name: Admin gating of UDF upload and plugin configuration
controls.description: Registering dynamic UDFs and configuring storage plugins are admin-gated operations that a plain SQL client cannot reach.

controls.name: Gated inbound impersonation
controls.description: A client cannot assume an arbitrary user identity via connection properties unless the operator configured a proxy/impersonation policy permitting it.

controls.name: Enable authentication and impersonation before multi-user exposure
controls.description: Enable authentication and impersonation before exposing Drill to more than one trusted user; do not run a multi-user cluster with the shipped auth-off / impersonation-off defaults.

controls.name: Lock down the Web UI / REST (:8047)
controls.description: The Web UI / REST endpoint can configure storage plugins and upload UDFs; restrict it to admins and protect it with authentication and TLS.

controls.name: Restrict plugin-config and UDF-upload rights
controls.description: Restrict who can configure storage plugins and upload dynamic UDFs to trusted admins; these are code and connectivity execution surfaces, and granting them to untrusted users hands over code execution and arbitrary connectivity.

controls.name: Configure wire encryption
controls.description: Configure wire encryption (SASL / SSL-TLS) on client-to-Drillbit and inter-Drillbit links on untrusted networks.

controls.name: Network-isolate the cluster and ZooKeeper
controls.description: Network-isolate the Drillbit cluster and ZooKeeper from untrusted networks, and give data-source credentials least privilege.

controls.name: Scope storage plugins narrowly
controls.description: Do not configure dfs/http/jdbc plugins broadly (filesystem root, open egress) and expose them to low-privilege query clients without impersonation; the plugin scope is the operator's boundary on query-driven file and network reach.
